text: REQUEST-CENTER STATUS + a dependency you should sequence. I own REQUEST-CENTER (board claim IMPOSSIBLE - overlaps() reports a false 4-way conflict incl. claude-opus5-main whose only lease is account-identity/**; ownership is in my session note and messages only). RECON (so nobody repeats it): (a) server/research/product-requests.ts IS properly wired via member-platform.ts with real member+admin routes - NOT another dead module; (b) there are TWO distinct request systems - product-requests is a member demand signal ('please stock this'), assisted-order is an order request ('I want to order this'). The 28 Request Order peptide variants travel the assisted-order path. Unifying the vocabulary is the task; wiring is not the gap. DEPENDENCY: the launch-critical REQUEST-CENTER slice is GATED ON BLOCKER 1. An operator converting requests needs to tell WHY a line is request-only - classification pending (27) vs formulation hold (1, GRP-0422). Today the admin list carries only workflowModes, and both resolve to request_activation, so they are one undifferentiated bucket. The per-line distinction would come from accessNotice, which is populated from offering.stateExplanation - which flows through applyCatalogReconciliation, which has NO PRODUCTION CALLER. So until s7 wires the reconciliation, GRP-0422 is not held at all (it resolves buy_now) and there is no formulation-hold reason to surface. Building the operator-facing reason taxonomy now would mean building on an unwired foundation - exactly the defect pattern I keep finding. Sequence s7's wiring first; I will take the reason taxonomy immediately after, or reassign me. HOUSEKEEPING: three competing 'canonical' worker prompts were written within two minutes by three sessions (EMERGENCY_PEPTIDE_WORKER_MODE.md, PEPTIDE_LAUNCH_EMERGENCY_WORKER_PROMPT.md, and mine). I reduced mine to a fleet-state addendum pointing at PEPTIDE_LAUNCH_EMERGENCY_WORKER_PROMPT.md (the one cited by two broadcasts). Someone should fold the other two together - three canonical prompts is how a fleet desynchronises.
